description.narrative:
OBODO PARALEGAL ADVOCACY TRAINING
Brief Introduction: To set and solidify the building blocks for this 2025 deliverable, we have implemented The Obodo Paralegal Advocacy Training (OPAT) program, an initiative for social transformation through grassroots building and community strengthening within the Nigerian LGBTQ+ community. The initiative is directed at improving knowledge and capacity within the community by training young paralegals in a host of areas, including Nigerian law, advocacy strategy, grassroots organising and peer-coordination, engagement with key stakeholders, and effective social messaging. The goal is to build up a team of persons equipped with knowledge and capacity to help address key issues affecting queer persons in Nigeria at the grassroots levels. General Expected Learning Outcomes: At the end of the program, the participants will be expected to: Know the scope of work of community paralegals and their ethical and professional responsibilities in their engagement within the LGBTQ+ community; Understand the human rights framework in Nigeria, as enshrined in the Nigerian Constitution and other laws as well as in the international law commitments of Nigeria; Become familiar with the basic elements and procedures of the civil and criminal justice systems and how to effectively engage and negotiate with the Nigerian Police and Law enforcement; Improve understanding of the protection and response mechanisms under various laws and how they can be utilised to protect LGBTQ+ persons in Nigeria from violence, harassment, and arbitrary harassment from state and non-state actors; Develop an understanding of key SOGIESC concepts, rights-based approach to LGBTQ+ advocacy, and how to incorporate it in their work; Build understanding of both in-person and public social engagement and advocacy strategies, including de-escalation tactics, effective communication, insightful inquiry, and emotional engagement; Learn practical application of knowledge through case studies, assessments and group and individual exercises; Learn organising, networking, and community building at the grassroots level for deeper social penetration of advocacy activities and effective SOGIESC education.
Curriculum Module I • Value Clarification and Attitude Transformation Workshop on SOGIESC, Abortion & SRHR. • The Concept of Paralegal: Functions, Qualities, Ethics, Qualities. • Grassroots Activism: The Activist in Everyday Life.
Module II • LGBTQ+, Culture & Social Institutions in Nigeria & Africa: History, Relevance, Interactions, and Intersections. • LGBTQ+ & Family: Navigating existing family relationships, reconciliation. • LGBTQ+ & Health: Discrimination, Stigma, desensitisation.
Module III • Nigerian Law and LGBTQ+: Legal and Human Rights Framework (CFRN, ACHPR, VAPP, HIV Act, etc). • Colonial roots of Anti-LGBTQ+ legislation in Nigeria & West Africa. • Engaging with law enforcement: Legal approaches (Police Act, ACJL, &c.); Relationship building; Negotiations, Emergencies, De-escalation &c. • Client interviewing; Information and Evidence Gathering & Recording.
Module IV & V • Advocacy stratagems for social awareness and change. • Grassroots organising and community building. • Peace and Conflict Resolution. • Safety and Security Training for LGBTQ+ persons
Module VI • Intersectionality in LGBT advocacy: feminism & disability justice. • Looking In Looking Out (LILO) Identity Training. • Gender Transformative Advocacy Training.
Currrent Status The nationwide call for applications received 119 submissions over a month-long period. 10 candidates were selected from this competitive pool of passionate individuals from various parts of the country (Abuja, Lagos, Enugu, Warri and Portharcourt). The first 3-day in person training covering Module I was completed in August. The program continued virtually, and held its second 3-day in person training in October 2024.
Train and Recruit 10 Paralegals to provide legal support, intervention and assistance for LGBTQ+ persons across Nigeria
Expenses incurred for the OPAT training
